info.name: ShortcutsBridge
info.subtitle: Run your Apple Shortcuts
info.subtitleNote: Subtitle MUST be 30 characters or fewer (OpenAI validates this). This is 24.
info.description: ShortcutsBridge connects ChatGPT to the Apple Shortcuts on your Mac. Ask what shortcuts you have, search them by name, and — with your confirmation — run one and get its result back in chat: "Run my Morning Briefing", "Run Log Water with 500", "What shortcuts are in my Home folder?". Because a Shortcut can do almost anything (control HomeKit, drive other apps, run scripts, call web APIs), this turns ChatGPT into a trigger for any automation you've already built. Your shortcuts never live on our servers: every action runs on your own Mac through a small open-source agent you install with one command (npx shortcuts-agent), and the relay only carries each request for the seconds it's in flight. ChatGPT always confirms before running a shortcut, and it can only run shortcuts you already created. Open source (MIT) and self-hostable.
info.developerIdentityNote: Substring matched against the verified identities in the dropdown (Business — Dupree Ops LLC). Identity verification already completed for the earlier Mac Bridge submissions.
info.demoRecordingNote: REQUIRED by OpenAI. YouTube (Unlisted). Demo arc against the reviewer library: list_shortcuts → list_folders → search_shortcuts (focus) → run_shortcut (Morning Briefing, confirmed) → run_shortcut (Log Water, input 600, confirmed) — shows ChatGPT's native Allow card naming the exact action + input.

domainVerification.note: The MCP section issues a token you must serve at /.well-known/openai-apps-challenge on the MCP hostname. server/api/challenge.js serves it from the OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE env var. Set it on Vercel (`vercel env add OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE production`), redeploy, then click Verify Domain. The token is a PUBLIC value, not a secret.

reviewerDemo.note: Reviewers use these to test the app 24/7 with no Mac (demo mode). The account authenticates on the OAuth consent page with email + password; the password lives in ../.env.local, never in this file. Enter the same values verbatim in the Testing section's Test credentials box. The demo account serves a server-side FICTIONAL Shortcuts library (isolated per user); run_shortcut returns realistic canned output, so nothing on a real device is ever touched and every tool is exercisable.

promptsNote: Up to 3 showcase prompts (Prompts section). They render as @Plugin chat bubbles.

testCases.expected: Returns the demo library's 7 shortcuts by name — Morning Briefing, Directions Home, Set a Timer, Start Focus, Daily Standup, Movie Night, Log Water (with a count of 7).

testCases.prompt: What folders are my shortcuts organized into?
testCases.expected: Returns the four folders: Daily, Home, Health, Work.
Finds 'Start Focus'. (list_shortcuts with a query does the same filtering.)

ChatGPT confirms first, then run_shortcut returns Morning Briefing's output: a weather line (Cupertino, sunny, ~68°F) plus a 3-event calendar summary (Standup 9:30, Design review 1:00, Dentist 4:15) and the top reminder.
ChatGPT confirms, then run_shortcut passes input 600 and returns 'Logged 600 ml. Today: 1600 ml of your 2,000 ml goal.' — showing the input flowed into the shortcut.

testCasesNote: Testing section requires EXACTLY 5 positive test cases; run against the seeded demo Shortcuts library. run_shortcut returns canned output, so nothing on a real device is touched.

negativeTestCases.scenario: A general question about automating a morning routine in the abstract — not a request to run a specific Apple Shortcut the user already has. There is nothing to list or run, so ShortcutsBridge should not trigger.
negativeTestCases.prompt: How should I automate my morning routine?

negativeTestCases.scenario: The user refers to a different automation platform. ShortcutsBridge only works with Apple Shortcuts on the user's Mac and should not trigger for Zapier, IFTTT, Make, or similar.
negativeTestCases.prompt: Set up a Zap that posts new emails to Slack.

negativeTestCases.scenario: A reminders or notes action, not a shortcut. ShortcutsBridge lists and runs Apple Shortcuts only; it should not trigger to add a reminder or write a note.
negativeTestCases.prompt: Add milk to my grocery reminders.

negativeTestCasesNote: Testing section requires EXACTLY 3 negative test cases (prompts where the app should NOT trigger).
releaseNotes: Initial release. ShortcutsBridge connects ChatGPT to your Apple Shortcuts through a small open-source agent that runs on your own Mac — list and search your shortcuts, and (with your confirmation) run one and get its result back in chat, optionally passing text input. Because a Shortcut can drive HomeKit, other apps, scripts, and web APIs, this makes ChatGPT a trigger for any automation you've already built. ChatGPT always confirms before running, and only shortcuts you created can run. Your shortcuts never live on our servers; the cloud piece is only a stateless relay. Open source (MIT) and self-hostable.
